acknowledgements.reason: Owner decision (b), 2026-10-09: the js target uses the exact lazy ring positions too, so the fast-ring patch is removed and its rewrite of the generateRingPositions search lambda leaves the js lock. It returned each concentric-ring start chunk without vanilla's biome search and moved 699 of 768 stronghold positions (6 seeds, structure-rings-parity.mjs against the old patch). patchChunkGeneratorStructureStateBrowserLazyRings replaces it on both targets (next entry).

Owner decision (b), 2026-10-09: the js target applies the lazy ring positions as the wasmgc target does (BrowserRingPositions moved to the shared sources, compiled for both TeaVM targets). generateRingPositions keeps vanilla's loop, RNG draws and search lambda with its forked RandomSource; only the supplyAsync submission of each search and Util.sequence become BrowserRingPositions.defer and .sequence, so every search runs once, lazily. JVM parity 768/768 positions and 9558/9558 contains() answers identical to vanilla on 6 seeds x 3 profiles (structure-rings-parity.mjs --target js). The frozen JS dists get the change with the v0.4.0 rebuild.

Reviewed 2026-10-28 against the clean profile bytecode: EnderDragonPhase registers these eleven classes in this order and invokes each public EnderDragon constructor. Direct dispatch preserves phase IDs and constructors while removing only unavailable reflection metadata; unknown IDs still fail with Error.

Owner decision, 2026-10-14: restore vanilla duplicate-UUID handling, so patchPersistentEntityUuidBrowserRecovery is removed on every profile and target. It rewrote PersistentEntitySectionManager.addEntityUuid to re-randomize a duplicate entity's UUID (up to 8 tries) and keep the entity, where vanilla rejects it with the 'UUID of added entity already exists' warning. It was added for duplicates that came from a TeaVM stream spliterator bug which loaded the last entity of each NBT entity list twice (<work-dir>/dupent/REPORT.md); that bug is fixed in the integration branch (dc68c26d), so the patch now only hides real duplicates. The vanilla class is no longer rewritten; frozen JavaScript output changes by this removal and is rebuilt at release.

Owner-requested UI change: remove only the offline insecure-server chat warning toast while preserving the seen-warning state, chat transport, validation and every other toast. The rewrite is limited to the vanilla ClientPacketListener toast submission.

Reviewed 2026-10-26: the title text still uses the build-injected release version, while the short lower-right About button is kept within the title bounds and opens BrowserAboutScreen through the vanilla widget callback.

Reviewed 2026-10-25 after the titletext integration: the patch retains the vanilla title screen fast-menu and Realms behavior while removing the browser-inapplicable profile, language, and accessibility icon row and routing the version/about text through BrowserAboutScreen. The static-write set is unchanged; the JavaScript target remains vanilla-exact apart from these documented browser UI changes.

Reviewed 2026-10-28 by vanilla-semantics review: the combined TitleScreen browser patch preserves vanilla button flow and semantics. Fast-menu changes remain limited to browser UI adaptation. In the browser Quit Game action, the patch replaces the synchronous vanilla Minecraft.stop() call with BrowserSingleplayerClient.quit(). Vanilla stop() tears down the client and integrated singleplayer server synchronously; the browser quit barrier performs the equivalent browser-owned save/world-close sequence first (worker stop acknowledgement, persistent-storage flush and close, lease release), then publishes the localized stopped page and asynchronously releases Wasm/graphics resources. This avoids a WasmGC renderer freeze while preserving the saved world and terminal state. No static-write set changes.

The worldgen patch now adds the recorded carver NoiseChunk seam required by the 26.2 fast terrain integration; the JVM 20/20 and 441/441 all-fields regressions remain passing, and the 26.2 WasmGC path keeps the existing NOISE-to-SURFACE lifetime contract.

Reviewed 2026-10-28 against the clean profile bytecode: EnderDragonPhase registers these eleven classes in this order and invokes each public EnderDragon constructor. Owner decision, 2026-10-14: restore vanilla duplicate-UUID handling, so patchPersistentEntityUuidBrowserRecovery is removed on every profile and target. It rewrote PersistentEntitySectionManager.addEntityUuid to re-randomize a duplicate entity's UUID (up to 8 tries) and keep the entity, where vanilla rejects it with the 'UUID of added entity already exists' warning. It was added for duplicates that came from a TeaVM stream spliterator bug which loaded the last entity of each NBT entity list twice (<work-dir>/dupent/REPORT.md); that bug is fixed in the integration branch (dc68c26d), so the patch now only hides real duplicates. The vanilla class is no longer rewritten; frozen JavaScript output changes by this removal and is rebuilt at release.

Owner-requested UI change: remove only the offline insecure-server chat warning toast while preserving the seen-warning state, chat transport, validation and every other toast. The rewrite is limited to the vanilla ClientPacketListener toast submission.

Reviewed 2026-10-26: the title text still uses the build-injected release version, while the short lower-right About button is kept within the title bounds and opens BrowserAboutScreen through the vanilla widget callback.

Reviewed 2026-10-28 by vanilla-semantics review: the combined TitleScreen browser patch preserves vanilla button flow and semantics. Fast-menu changes remain limited to browser UI adaptation. In the browser Quit Game action, the patch replaces the synchronous vanilla Minecraft.stop() call with BrowserSingleplayerClient.quit(). Vanilla stop() tears down the client and integrated singleplayer server synchronously; the browser quit barrier performs the equivalent browser-owned save/world-close sequence first (worker stop acknowledgement, persistent-storage flush and close, lease release), then publishes the localized stopped page and asynchronously releases Wasm/graphics resources. This avoids a WasmGC renderer freeze while preserving the saved world and terminal state. No static-write set changes.

The worldgen patch now adds the recorded lazy NoiseChunk carver seam required by the 26.3 fast terrain integration; JVM 20/20 and 441/441 worldgen regressions remain passing, and the browser kernel remains default-off pending the release gate.
